pillar_reactions.evidence: Engaged and asked twice to understand the mechanics. First he checked the feedback loop back to the rep: 'this first phase will be the three four times the week trainings, but for that I will need to send some kind of videos. Trevor can correct me the way I'm doing it in a technical way.' Then he asked a specific programming question: 'is there a way that I can maybe work more or empathize in some kind of maybe lower body?... for me my core is very important because this is what keeps me standing up while maybe the 11th hour.' He was answered with 'it's a completely customized program' and routed to the Trevor onboarding call.

Pushed back on the substance of the fasting component, and for a specific reason: 'My dad passed away 15 years ago, but he was in a mistreatment about diabetes. So I have this... pain in my mind that it's not a fear, but it's kind of a thing that I'm kind of want to move away from, the fasting thing, because that affects into the insulin and the pancreas and that stuff.' The rep did not defer the question; he answered it by describing his own practice — 'My dad also suffers from diabetes as well, but I do pretty extensive fasting protocols at least a couple of times a month', longest fast 72 hours, 'it feels like something divine is happening.' The objection was parked rather than resolved: 'that will be maybe my first questions for Trevor.'

Volunteered a positive reaction and tied it directly to his own framing of the purchase: 'Yeah, that's the thing I was thinking. You're teaching the people to get their own lifestyle. That's what I was starting with. This is my lifestyle.' The no-subscription positioning ('we're not like other programs out there that run a subscription model') landed hardest of anything in the pitch, because it matched the complaint he had already made about Instagram programmes.

anchors.raw: I have, with me, the expertise of a nutritionist, a physiologist, a mind, well, it's my therapist, but the mind therapist, a running coach, and I'm missing that weight.
anchors.competitor: His own nutritionist, exercise physiologist, running coach and therapist
anchors.note: Cuts both ways and the rep only ever saw one side. Supportively, this is a man with an established habit of paying multiple experts, which normally makes price a non-issue. Operationally it undercut, because two of the three pillars duplicate services he already funds and he said so: 'I don't want to double the spend in something I already have' and 'I'm spending a lot of Mexican pesos here.' The offer is priced as a whole-life system to a man who has already bought most of the system piecemeal.

anchors.raw: I'm seeing some of the training programs out there in Instagram and they're not always delivers what they say, or maybe it's okay, this is a one-time payment for life, and they just upload some training sets or something or et cetera. But there's not this one-on-one sessions that we can improve the way you're doing
anchors.note: The one genuinely supportive anchor on the call. He had already tried and dismissed the cheap category and articulated exactly why the expensive one is different — human review of his form. This is the strongest value hook available and the rep did draw it out with 'what gives you the most confidence', but never converted it into price justification when the number landed.

anchors.raw: I'm not meant to really recommend this, but we have something called Love It or Leave It. So one-week trial, it's only 1,200 bucks
anchors.note: A rep-created anchor that reset the entire negotiation. Once $1,200 exists, the $4,000, $6,000 and $9,000 tiers are all reframed as optional escalations rather than as the product. Note the sequence: the prospect had already said 'for sure, it's worth it' and was leaning to three months; the discount was not extracted from the rep, it was volunteered.

anchors.raw: for this exchange matter, I will do for sure my credit card because of the dollars and stuff. And then maybe I can split that into maybe three months, so I can do my overall month spend and see if I can get it.
anchors.note: USD pricing against peso income adds an FX layer the offer does not acknowledge. Worth noting at corpus level — this prospect reached for self-financing across three months unprompted and the rep did not pick it up, which is a missed instalment close that would have preserved full price.

unmet_demand.want: A training-only engagement that does not duplicate the nutritionist, physiologist, running coach and therapist he already pays for
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is a fixed three-pillar bundle at one price. There is no reduced-scope tier, and the rep's only concession on the point was 'we're not here to overhaul anything' on nutrition, which reduces the value of a pillar without reducing the price. The objection was still unresolved at the moment of agreement.

unmet_demand.want: Nutrition guidance that accounts for a family history of diabetes — specifically whether fasting protocols are appropriate for someone with his paternal history and concerns about insulin and pancreatic function
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep answered a health question with personal anecdote (his own 72-hour fasts, his own father's diabetes) rather than deferring it, and the question was then parked for Trevor. Whether the programme can or should adapt its fasting protocols on medical-history grounds, and who is qualified to make that call, is unestablished.

unmet_demand.want: Discipline-specific emphasis — lower body and core loading tuned to holding form at the eleventh hour of an ultra, rather than general full-body kettlebell work
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Probably served: the rep asserted full customisation and routed it to the Trevor onboarding call. But nothing was shown, no ultra-endurance precedent was cited, and the answer rested entirely on a promise. Given the prospect's November race this is the feature the retention of the account depends on.

unmet_demand.want: Clarity on what the $1,200 product actually is — how long it lasts, what happens at the end, and on what terms he can walk away
unmet_demand.why_unmet: It was described as a 'one-week trial' and, one sentence later, as ending 'at the end of the one month'. No written terms, no refund mechanism and no reconciliation of the two durations were given before he said yes.
